description: Minerva pro-grade MCP pentesting attack pack. 30 attacks covering every documented MCP attack surface (Client / Server / Data-in-Transit). All parameters are UI-dynamic — pentesters tune timeouts, transport, protocol version, payload tags, encoding modes, and target scoping at run-time.

attacks.name: Direct Prompt Injection (Pro)
attacks.description: Canary-verified prompt injection across every MCP tool. Pulls the full payload library (zero-width split, Cyrillic confusables, RTL override, multilingual, Claude/GPT/markdown variants). Confirmed findings require the canary to appear in the tool response.

payload_tags.title: Extra payload-library tags (AND)
payload_tags.description: Filter the payload library further. e.g. ['zero_width','rtl_override']

attacks.name: Indirect Prompt Injection (Pro)
attacks.description: Audits MCP resources, prompts, and resource templates for hostile directives. Tests tool-output echoing to confirm attacker strings reflect into client context. Subscribes to resources to detect server-pushed prompt poisoning.

attacks.name: Tool Poisoning (Pro)
attacks.description: Static + active audit of MCP tool / prompt / resource metadata. Detects zero-width unicode, HTML comments, fake deprecation, role-switch directives, RTL override. Then ACTIVELY calls the poisoned tool to verify the directive influenced output (confidence promotion).

active_exploitation.title: Actively call poisoned tools
active_exploitation.description: Promotes findings from 'high' to 'confirmed' when directive influences output.

attacks.name: Tool Shadowing & TOCTOU (Pro)
attacks.description: Detects tool-name collisions, description duplication, and TOCTOU drift across multiple tools/list snapshots. Optionally exercises ambiguous tools to record which implementation answers — exploitation proof, not just detection.

exploit_collisions.title: Exploit name collisions
exploit_collisions.description: Call colliding tool names to record routing.

attacks.name: Command Injection (Pro)
attacks.description: Three-layer detection: timing-based blind, OOB-callback confirmed, and adaptive encoding-bypass mutation (IFS, base64, env-var, null-byte). Auto baseline measurement; PowerShell + lolbin payloads on Windows hosts.

tool_keywords.title: Tool-name keywords
tool_keywords.description: Override the default keyword list for candidate selection.

attacks.name: SQL Injection (Pro)
attacks.description: Four-layer SQLi: error-based DB fingerprint, boolean-based, time-based per-dialect (MySQL/PG/MSSQL/Oracle/SQLite), WAF bypass on retry (case/comment/tab). Confidence scales medium→confirmed.

attacks.name: Remote Code Execution (Pro)
attacks.description: OOB-confirmed RCE plus reverse-shell PoC. Tries Python/Node/PHP/Ruby/Java payloads + SSTI (Jinja/SpEL) + Log4Shell JNDI. Falls back to timing detection where egress is blocked.

attacks.name: SSRF (Pro)
attacks.description: OOB-confirmed SSRF on URL-accepting tools. Modern cloud-metadata probes (AWS IMDSv2 token flow, GCP Metadata-Flavor header, Azure scope params, OCI/Alibaba/DO/Hetzner). Plus K8s SA token, Docker socket, etcd/consul, gopher Redis.

url_keywords.title: URL-param keywords
url_keywords.description: Override default keyword set for URL-tool detection.

attacks.name: Path Traversal / LFI (Pro)
attacks.description: Confirms path traversal via canonical markers across Linux + Windows + /proc/self + cloud-creds files. Adaptive encoding-bypass retry (URL, double, UTF-8 overlong, null-byte, unicode).

attacks.name: Authentication Bypass (Pro)
attacks.description: Auth/no-auth/bad-token comparison + JWT alg=none / kid SQLi / weak-HMAC tests + per-tool authorization probing. Detects token oracles via error-text differential.

attacks.name: Tool Rebinding (Pro)
attacks.description: Functional TOCTOU race: tools/list → exercise each → tools/list again. Flags tools that appear/disappear/mutate. Optionally tests sampling/createMessage to see if rebound tools auto-call.

attacks.name: Resource Exhaustion / DoS (Pro)
attacks.description: Non-destructive DoS audit: oversized arg, deep nesting, concurrency burst with rate-limit-header inspection, latency degradation curve, ReDoS catastrophic-backtracking probe. Measures impact, doesn't tip the target over.

attacks.name: Information Disclosure (Pro)
attacks.description: Multi-surface leakage audit. Discovered secrets are VALIDATED against issuer endpoints (AWS STS, GitHub /user, Slack auth.test, OpenAI/Anthropic /models) — confidence is promoted to 'confirmed' only when the secret authenticates. JWT structure analysed for alg=none / weak-HMAC.

validate_secrets.title: Validate found secrets against issuer
validate_secrets.description: Sends safe identity-only requests (e.g. STS GetCallerIdentity) to confirm secrets are real.

attacks.name: LLM Jailbreak (Pro)
attacks.description: Multi-template safety-bypass corpus (DAN, grandma, hypothetical, delimiter-escape, base64, refusal-override) + adaptive escalation: each refusal triggers a stronger template. Confirms via canary + unsafe-marker co-occurrence.

attacks.name: Insecure Deserialization (Pro)
attacks.description: Tests pickle, YAML, Java preamble (AC ED 00 05), .NET BinaryFormatter sinks. Three-phase proof: canary, unsafe load, OOB-confirmed pickle (RCE via __reduce__).

attacks.name: MCP MITM & Data-in-Transit Posture (Pro)
attacks.description: Enterprise transit audit: plain-HTTP probe, TLS chain validation, version + cipher score, ALPN/SNI, HSTS/CSP/X-Frame, weak-cipher negotiation, secret leakage in tool responses.

attacks.name: OAuth 2.1 Flow Attacks (Pro)
attacks.description: MCP 2025-06-18 mandates OAuth 2.1. Audits .well-known metadata, redirect-URI validation, PKCE enforcement, state requirement, token-endpoint client-auth bypass (alg=none JWT), audience confusion, scope laxity, bearer-token error oracles.

attacks.name: Sampling Abuse (Pro)
attacks.description: MCP `sampling/createMessage` is a client capability — servers should never advertise it nor respond to it. This attack tests capability advertising, reverse sampling probe (send to server), tool-induced sampling injection, and prompt-template delegation language.

attacks.name: Elicitation Abuse (Pro)
attacks.description: MCP 2025-06-18 elicitation/create lets the server ask the user for input. Tests capability mis-advertising, reverse elicitation probe, sensitive-field detection (password/api_key/OTP), and tool-output phishing language.

attacks.name: Prompts Argument Injection (Pro)
attacks.description: Targets the prompts/get template surface. Canary verification + SSTI engines (Jinja2/Velocity/Handlebars/Mustache/EL/Razor/Twig) + role-message override + schema-laxity (extra/undeclared args).

attacks.name: Stdio Argv / Env Injection (Pro)
attacks.description: Stdio-transport-specific. Probes argv splitting (newline/null/IFS), shell-variable expansion ($HOME / %PATH%), and env / process leakage (/proc/self/environ, $ENV).

attacks.name: Schema Type Confusion (Pro)
attacks.description: Type-mismatch fuzzing of tool inputSchema: wrong-type values, numeric overflow, deep JSON nesting, extra-property handling, required-field omission, oneOf/anyOf polymorphic confusion.

attacks.name: Pagination Cursor Abuse (Pro)
attacks.description: Opaque-cursor abuse on tools/list, resources/list, prompts/list, resources/templates/list. Tests SQLi/path-traversal/SSRF via cursor, oversized cursor DoS, type-confusion, and structural disclosure (decodable cursors leak DB internals).

attacks.name: Tool Annotations Spoofing (Pro)
attacks.description: MCP-novel. Verifies the honesty of tool annotation hints (readOnlyHint / destructiveHint / idempotentHint / openWorldHint). Calls each tool claimed read-only with safe args, snapshots resources/list before+after, and reports any state-drift as a CONFIRMED lie. Also flags contradictory hints, missing destructiveHint on destructively-named tools, and missing openWorldHint on URL-accepting tools.

attacks.name: Logging setLevel Abuse (Pro)
attacks.description: Abuses the MCP `logging/setLevel` control-plane RPC. Tests unauthenticated acceptance, post-flip secret leakage in tool-error responses, non-standard level acceptance, and undeclared-capability acceptance. Promotes to CONFIRMED when secrets / stack-traces / SQL queries appear in responses after flipping to debug.

probe_tools_after_debug.title: Probe tools after debug flip for leakage

attacks.name: Authorization Horizontal — BOLA/IDOR (Pro)
attacks.description: OWASP API #1. Discovers tools with ID-shaped parameters (id, user_id, owner, file_id, document_id, ...) and probes for missing object-level authorization. Single-principal mode mutates IDs heuristically; two-principal mode (with secondary_auth) cross-calls primary→secondary's resources for CONFIRMED IDOR.

secondary_auth.title: Secondary auth (two-principal mode)
secondary_auth.description: auth_config dict for a second principal. Empty = single-principal mode.

attacks.name: Notifications & Subscription Abuse (Pro)
attacks.description: Tests MCP server-pushed channels: resources/subscribe acceptance without resources.subscribe capability, unbounded subscription flooding, subscribe to non-existent URI without validation, and malformed notifications/* handling. Flags stack-trace leakage from poorly-handled notifications.

attacks.name: WebSocket Transport Hardening (Pro)
attacks.description: WebSocket-transport-specific hardening checks. Issues raw HTTP upgrades (not via MCPClient) to verify Origin header validation (CSWSH), Sec-WebSocket-Protocol negotiation strictness, and acceptance of upgrades without HTTP-layer Authorization on auth-configured targets.

attacks.name: HTTP Session Hardening (Pro)
attacks.description: HTTP / streamable-HTTP transport-specific. Audits Set-Cookie flags (HttpOnly / Secure / SameSite), session fixation (server accepts attacker-supplied session before auth), session-ID predictability (Shannon entropy across N samples), and Mcp-Session-Id binding (server accepts arbitrary tampered values).

attacks.name: Protocol Version Downgrade (Pro)
attacks.description: Negotiates every known MCP protocol version against the server. Flags acceptance of deprecated versions (lacking OAuth 2.1, elicitation), bogus future versions, mid-session re-init, and JSON-RPC batch (removed in 2025-03-26).
